name: Biochemical Basis of Disease and Cellular Compartmentalization

reference.source: Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry / Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry
clinicalPearls: Metabolic compartmentalization separates anabolic cytosolic pathways from catabolic mitochondrial matrix reactions
Inner mitochondrial membrane is impermeable to ions and polar solutes, preserving the electrochemical proton gradient
Enzyme deficiencies cause proximal toxic substrate accumulation and distal essential product depletion
Peroxisomes initiate beta-oxidation of very long-chain fatty acids (C22 or longer) and synthesize plasmalogens
Zellweger syndrome results from defective peroxisomal biogenesis (PEX mutations), causing death in early infancy
reference.pathophysiology: Spatial segregation within subcellular organelles prevents futile metabolic cycling and enables independent allosteric control. Inborn errors of metabolism arise from loss-of-function mutations in compartment-specific enzymes, resulting in failure of energetic product generation and toxic accumulation of upstream intermediates. Disruption of peroxisomal protein import causes multi-organ developmental failure.
additionalDifferentials: Classical galactosemia and hereditary fructose intolerance
additionalInvestigations: Plasma amino acid chromatography and acylcarnitine profile via tandem mass spectrometry
Urine organic acid analysis by gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS)
Plasma very long-chain fatty acid (VLCFA) levels (elevated C26:0 and C26:1)
Blood lactate, pyruvate, and ammonia to distinguish mitochondrial vs urea cycle defects
